kind: ADDITIVE and IMMUTABLE. A reconstruction of the HISTORICAL July imitative protocol from the production sources and the July reports, pinned by content. July is METHOD ONLY: no July checkpoint, dataset, label or anchor is ever used

target_domain_dagger.py.role: the July CLI whose argparse defaults fix the hyperparameters

target_domain_markov_adaptation.py.role: the 13/07 Markov stage; not used by the base phase

loss_transcribed_from_production.anchor_loss: torch.stack([(p - anchor[name]).square().mean() for name, p in module.pi.named_parameters() if p.requires_grad]).mean()

early_stopping_transcribed_from_producti.rule: val_mse < best_validation_mse - 1e-9 updates best, best_epoch and a deepcopy of pi.state_dict, and resets the stale counter; otherwise the stale counter increments

production_capabilities_that_match_this_.hard_zero_first_layer_features: production already projects arbitrary first-layer columns to exact zero after every step. This is exactly the masking mechanism the base phase needs, and it is NOT an invention of this branch
production_capabilities_that_match_this_.freeze_logstd_head: production already supports hard-freezing the log-std head
production_capabilities_that_match_this_.training_indices_validation_indices: production already accepts an EXPLICIT split, which is what leave-one-trajectory-out requires
production_capabilities_that_match_this_.selection_mode_fixed_final_epoch: production already supports training a fixed number of epochs with no validation, which is what the final all-data fit requires

why_this_branch_reimplements_the_fit_in_.reason: production adapt_actor loads its input with RLModule.from_checkpoint, the RLlib checkpoint format. Every artifact of this project is exported in the warm_start rl_module format instead, and all eight previous fits of this bridge used the in-sandbox fit for that reason
why_this_branch_reimplements_the_fit_in_.mitigation: the sandbox loss and per-step order are pinned against the production block above and verified by a differential test, term by term, on random inputs

logstd_weight.note: kept for fidelity. With a constant-sigma head whose log-std weight rows are zero, the log-std output does not depend on the trunk, so this term contributes exactly zero gradient to every trainable weight that survives the step, and the head is restored after every step anyway. The receipt verifies the head is byte-identical after the fit

validation_split.july: seeded random permutation over the aggregate (validation_fraction 0.20)
validation_split.why: the July random split leaks temporal neighbours; production already supports explicit indices

hard_zero_columns.july_base: not used in the 11/07 DAgger path
hard_zero_columns.here: the ten controller columns and the two clock columns, zeroed after every step
hard_zero_columns.why: the base phase of this branch masks the controller channel by design

deterministic_algorithms.why: stricter, and consistent with the in-sandbox fit used by every previous stage of this bridge

final_fit.here: three leave-one-trajectory-out folds for epoch selection, then one final fit on all rows for the median best epoch with no validation
final_fit.why: preregistered by the architect before any fit
